html:
The Cimmerians were horse nomads of the steppe north of the Black Sea who raided deep into West Asia in the 700s and 600s BCE. The map spells them "Cimerians" and shows them from 1500 BCE, earlier than any record of them.

They spoke an Iranian language and lived much like the Scythians, who displaced them. They left no writing; we know them from Assyrian letters and Greek authors. In Homer's Odyssey they live at the edge of the world in mist and darkness.

Pushed south across the Caucasus, they appear in history around 714 BCE, when they defeated the kingdom of Urartu, as reported to the Assyrian king. They then raided Anatolia. They overran Phrygia, whose king Midas, by Greek tradition, killed himself. In the 640s BCE they sacked Sardis, the capital of Lydia, and killed its king Gyges. Lydia finally defeated them under King Alyattes around 600 BCE, and they vanish from the record.
